content.text:
`python3 -m unittest -q` now passes: all 7 tests run with no failures. To get there I fixed two bugs in `household/bills.py` and changed one expected value in a test that was wrong.

**Code fixes in `household/bills.py`:**

1. **`split_bill` dropped the leftover cents.** It gave every person `total // people`, so 1001 split two ways came out as `[500, 500]` and a cent went missing. It now uses `divmod` and gives one extra cent to each of the first `remainder` people, which is what the docstring describes. 1001 split two ways is now `[501, 500]`.
2. **`due_dates` crashed when the dates crossed into a new year.** It added `i` to the month without wrapping, so it asked for month 13 and raised `IllegalMonthError`. It now uses `divmod(first.month - 1 + i, 12)` to roll the year forward and wrap the month back to 1.

**Test change in `tests/test_bills.py`:**

- `test_three_ways` expected `split_bill(1000, 3)` to return `[333, 333, 333]`, which adds up to 999, not 1000. That contradicts the docstring and the remainder test right next to it. It only passed because of the bug in point 1. I changed the expected value to `[334, 333, 333]`.

If you really did mean for the extra cent to be dropped in that case, tell me and I'll revert the test change. But then `split_bill` can't meet both that test and the remainder test, so one of them would have to change.

I haven't committed anything.
